A deep mossy canyon splitting the earth in a long green gash, its ferny walls dropping forty feet to a glowing turquoise stream, soft mist curling up between the dripping ledges in pale ribbons.
A tumbling four-tier waterfall cascading down a fern-draped cliff-face, each tier spilling into its own mossy basin before overflowing to the next, spray drifting in golden shafts of filtered light.
A winding glowing stream threading between mossy banks, its pale turquoise water rushing over smooth amber stones into deep still pools, the surface trembling with reflected leaf-light and soft foam.

A cluster of colossal moss-furred boulders, each one larger than a cottage, leaning together in a great tumbled heap, their gaps and hollows choked with fern and wildflower, soft green velvet on every surface.
A sheer mossy cliff-face rising sixty feet from a bed of ferns, its surface streaked with mineral rust and soft green fur, water seeping from unseen cracks and tracing silver lines down the stone.

A grove of colossal ancient trees, their trunks wider than four arms can reach, their roots arching from the earth like the legs of sleeping giants, the canopy so dense the air below is a green cathedral twilight.
A rocky river-island splitting a wide rushing stream, its surface crowned with moss and twisted willows, the water dividing around it in two bright channels that rejoin in a churning pool below.
A misty ravine barely wide enough to walk, its walls hung with cascading ferns and pale orchids, a thin stream threading the rocky floor far below, the air cool and dripping and green.

A sea-cliff plunging straight into turquoise water, its face streaked with salt and orange lichen, the surf booming in the caves at its base, spray rising high enough to wet the wildflowers at its lip.

A long tumbled rock-scree slope cascading down a hillside, the pale grey stones softened by decades of moss and creeping thyme, small ferns sprouting from every gap where soil has gathered between the rocks.

A wide cave-mouth opening in a moss-hung cliff, its interior glowing with pale bioluminescent growth, a thin stream running out across smooth stone at its threshold, the air inside cool and smelling of deep earth.
A chain of small rocky islets crossing a wide still lake, each one furred with moss and crowned with a single twisted pine, connected at low water by stepping-stone paths of pale rounded rock.

A cascade of terraced hot-spring pools stepping down a hillside, each basin rimmed with orange and cream mineral crust, the water steaming gently in cool air, the stone below stained vivid rust and jade.

A fern-choked rocky creek-bed winding between mossy boulders, the water so shallow it barely covers the amber stones, the banks dense with hart's-tongue and bracken bending over to touch across the stream.
A forested rocky outcrop rising from the valley floor like a blunt fist of stone, its sides draped in hanging fern and ivy, its summit a small flat crown of windswept moss and ancient twisted oak.

A deep glowing sinkhole dropping thirty feet into the earth, its circular walls furred entirely in moss and maidenhair fern, a pool of still turquoise water at the bottom reflecting the open sky above like a mirror.

A mossy gorge where two cliff-walls lean close overhead, the gap between them only a bright strip of sky, the stone floor below polished smooth by centuries of flood-water and scattered with pale oval stones.

A colossal standing pinnacle of black rock rising alone from a meadow of tall grass, its surface colonized by pale lichen and creeping fig, a single ancient tree somehow rooted in a crack near its summit.
A wide rocky grotto set into a hillside, its ceiling hung with roots and moss, a still shallow pool filling its floor, the water so clear each pebble beneath is sharp and bright as if magnified.

A long rapid running between high mossy banks, the white water breaking over submerged ledges and curling into foam-laced pools, the noise filling the whole valley so that speech must be raised to be heard.

A tilted shelf of ancient bedrock rising from a forest floor, its surface cracked in long parallel lines filled with soil and fern, the pale stone warm in filtered light, lichens painting it in maps of grey and gold.

A hanging garden of moss and fern draped from a high wet cliff above a quiet pool, the roots of wildflowers threading down the stone face, water weeping constantly from the overhang and beading on every leaf below.

A wide boulder-field beside a mountain river, the great stones rounded and pale, their upper surfaces cushioned with thick moss, the water running between them in narrow fast chutes and spreading into broad gravelled shallows beyond.

A half-submerged rock-arch rising from a still cove, its keystone draped in seaweed and sea-pink, the water beneath it glowing pale green in clear light, small waves folding quietly through the gap with a soft hollow sound.

A grove of immense ancient conifers growing from a steep rocky slope, their roots gripping the stone in great gnarled claws, their bark deep-furrowed and rust-red, the air between them still and resinous and full of soft gold light.
